clue.text: Reject sugar, bad, a carb: Atkins' somewhat tricky formula?

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the hidden letters are read in the opposite direction
only somewhat of the run of words is used, so the letters sit hidden inside them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of sugar into the start of Atkins

explanation.surface: A dieter on the Atkins plan turns down sugar and carbs as a bad, tricky recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reject' turns round the run ARBADACARBA found inside 'sugar, bad, a carb: Atkins'. The Atkins diet, which cuts carbohydrates, makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: The magic word of conjurors is a formula spoken while performing tricks, hence a tricky formula.

clue.text: Scottish writer is saving flood defences

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Iain ..., the Scottish novelist
second meaning: puts money in a bank, so is saving
third meaning: raised earth walls that hold back a river

explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings in a row: the novelist Iain Banks, a verb for depositing money, and river embankments.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a Scottish author, the act of depositing money, and earthworks along a river.

clue.text: It may be painful cracking complex cases with hollow bullets

indicators.note: the bullet letters crack open the other word and lodge inside
complex means intricate and tangled, so the letters are rearranged
a hollow word keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Cracking difficult cases with hollow-point bullets sounds a painful business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' rearranges CASES to ACESS, and 'hollow' leaves BS from 'bullets'; 'cracking' puts BS inside, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A swollen pocket of pus in the body tissue is typically sore and tender.

clue.text: Write from Paris to The Thunderer?

parts.note: au is French, as spoken in Paris, for to the
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: Writing a letter from Paris to The Times, nicknamed The Thunderer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thunderer is an old nickname for The Times newspaper, which makes the surface plausible; here it is the Norse god Thor.
explanation.definitionFit: To author a work is to compose it, which is a synonym of write.

clue.text: Warning: beer can start to get round resistance

indicators.note: the beer can letters go round the resistance letter, enclosing it

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a tin is a can

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A warning that a beer can is just beginning to go round the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Alerting someone is giving them notice of danger, the same as warning.

clue.text: Within reach of oarsmen with a sailor in place

indicators.note: the short letters are placed in the word for place, inside it

parts.note: a role is a position or place
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A rowing crew with a sailor in position, within reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be covered by rowing is navigable by oar, reachable by a crew.

clue.text: Resistance unit airmen set up to apply intelligence that baker could supply

indicators.note: in a down answer, set up means written upwards, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the ohm is the unit of electrical resistance
RAF is the Royal Air Force
to use is to apply
loaf means head or brains, from rhyming slang loaf of bread

explanation.surface: A wartime Resistance cell sets up airmen to use intelligence the baker could supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance unit' suggests the French Resistance but is the ohm. 'Use your loaf' is British slang for 'use your head', from rhyming slang loaf of bread for head.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmhouse loaf is a large, crusty white bread sold in bakeries.

clue.text: Nearly unconscious? Very unconscious and hardly observant

indicators.note: nearly a word means all but its last letter

parts.note: under, as in under anaesthetic, means unconscious
out, as in out cold, means unconscious

explanation.surface: Someone half asleep, then out cold, is hardly paying attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'observant' looks like attentive, but in the definition it means religiously observant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone undevout is not pious, barely keeping religious practices.

clue.text: Child angry about Arthur's dad's four-star arrangement

indicators.note: the son goes about the father's name, enclosing it

parts.note: a son is a child
Uther Pendragon is King Arthur's father in legend
cross means angry

explanation.surface: A child, cross about King Arthur's father, gets a four-star rating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'four-star' looks like a hotel rating; it means a pattern of four stars.
explanation.definitionFit: The Southern Cross is a constellation whose four bright stars form a cross shape.

clue.text: Saint's name through an eternity

indicators.note: the abbreviation for name goes through the middle of the other word, so it sits inside

parts.note: ages means a very long time, an eternity

explanation.surface: A saint's name has endured through the ages for an eternity.
explanation.definitionFit: St Agnes is a Roman virgin martyr, one of the best-known female saints.

clue.text: Fighter's moves do not wake bats

indicators.note: bats here is the adjective meaning crazy, so the words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A fighter warns that bats are not to be woken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the animals but is slang for mad, the signal to rearrange DO NOT WAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: This Korean martial art consists of the kicks and strikes a combatant performs.

clue.text: Spread fake news about Republican men in hazy situation

indicators.note: the short words go in the word for hazy situation, sitting inside it

parts.note: mist is a hazy condition of the air
OR, other ranks, stands for ordinary soldiers, i.e. men

explanation.surface: A commentator spreads fake news about Republicans while the picture remains murky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a containment signal but is only part of the surface 'spread fake news about'; 'in' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: To misreport is to give an inaccurate account, which is what spreading false news amounts to.

clue.text: Port, or what's left after opening of bottle

indicators.note: the remainder comes after the single letter in the answer
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the rest is what remains

explanation.surface: Choosing between port and whatever remains once a bottle has been opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' tempts as the drink in the bottle; here it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Brest is a major naval harbour city in Brittany, north-west France.

clue.text: It's over corporal, possibly way overhead

parts.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over
a corporal is one example of a non-commissioned officer, NCO
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A corporal who is far over the top, perhaps in the way of a costly overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: An oncost is a British accounting term for an overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: An oncost is a business expense not tied to production, in other words an overhead cost.

clue.text: How surprising to find whisky, say, in baby carriages?

indicators.note: the liquor is placed in the exclamation, inside it

parts.note: coo is a British exclamation of surprise
hooch is illicit or cheap liquor, of which whisky is an example

explanation.surface: Shock at finding whisky hidden in a baby's pram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baby carriages' suggests prams; it means a train, in a child's word.
explanation.definitionFit: Choo-choo is nursery talk for a railway train, so its carriages are a baby's train.

clue.text: What cheer is behind most of recognised desk space?

indicators.note: the exclamation words come behind, after, the shortened word
most of a word means all but its last letter

parts.note: knew means recognised, as in knew someone by sight
eh is an exclamation meaning what?
ole is a Spanish cheer of approval

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where the cheering sits relative to something largely recognised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What cheer' reads as one old greeting but is split: EH (what?) and OLE (a cheer), placed after KNE.
explanation.definitionFit: The recess under a desk where the sitter's legs go is the space for the knees.

clue.text: Feature of some altimeters showing when to fill up?

indicators.note: Feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pilot's instrument has a reading that tells when to refuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fill up' suggests refuelling an aircraft; it means eating.
explanation.definitionFit: The time for eating, when you fill your stomach, is when food is served.

clue.text: Ranchers displacing monks etc

indicators.note: displacing the letters moves them out of their places into a new order

explanation.surface: Ranchers moving monks and the like out of their homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Men who tend livestock on a ranch or farm are cattle handlers, synonymous with ranchers.

clue.text: Family band on the road for Mull

parts.note: kin is family
a tyre is a rubber band running on the road

explanation.surface: A family band touring the roads mulls things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mull' looks like the verb 'ponder'; the Mull of Kintyre is a headland in south-west Scotland, famous from Paul McCartney's song, which also fits 'band'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mull is a Scottish headland, and Kintyre's peninsula ends in the best-known one.

clue.text: Far from swarthy lot without a care

parts.note: wan means pale, the opposite of swarthy
a ton, as in tons of, means a lot

explanation.surface: A pale-faced bunch who haven't a worry in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanton behaviour is reckless and heedless, done without regard for consequences.

clue.text: I'll get people back up river such as one in Russia

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means read from the bottom, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
e.g. means for example, such as
the Neva is a river in Russia, flowing through St Petersburg

explanation.surface: A vow of revenge made going up a Russian river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like the reversal signal, but it belongs to the definition; 'up' turns the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who exacts revenge pays wrongdoers back for what they did.

clue.text: English team going up in place succeeded, getting points on display

indicators.note: the team letters go in the place letters, inside them

parts.note: PL is the street abbreviation for place

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means the letters run backwards

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team
S is short for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: An English team climbing in the table succeeds, getting points on the scoreboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' and 'team' make it read like a league table; the points are dots on a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Pixels are the tiny dots that make up an image on a screen.

clue.text: Facility for a listener and another missing person

indicators.note: the word is as heard by someone listening, so it sounds like the entry

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet, a facility
can is another slang word for a toilet

explanation.surface: Looking for toilet facilities and another person who has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Lucan is a British peer who vanished in 1974 after his children's nanny was murdered and was never found.
explanation.definitionFit: The earl disappeared without trace, making him Britain's most famous vanished individual.

clue.text: Sly look around island that's in French city

indicators.note: the sly look goes around the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a leer is a sly or knowing look
c'est is French for that is

explanation.surface: A sly glance at an island somewhere in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French city' tempts, but the definition is just 'city': Leicester is in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is a large city in the East Midlands of England.

clue.text: Kid in brief service of China

indicators.note: a brief word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a tea set is a china service

explanation.surface: A child in a short spell of service in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child; it is the verb, to tease. 'China' looks like the country but is porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid someone is to joke with or mock them playfully.

clue.text: Render identity void with no names?

definitions.text: Render identity void with no names?

parts.words: Render identity void with no names?
parts.note: removing all names from data so nobody can be identified

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes stripping names from records so a person cannot be traced.
explanation.definitionFit: To anonymise data is to remove identifying details so the subject cannot be recognised.

clue.text: Rat out of rice, e.g.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to inform on someone, British slang for snitching
second meaning: rice is an example of a cereal plant of the ... family

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a rat creeping out of rice; 'Rat out' and 'rice, e.g.' are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for an informer's betrayal and the botanical family that includes cereals.

clue.text: What you need in house following awkward scenes

indicators.note: the house comes after the rearranged letters
awkward suggests the letters are clumsily arranged, to be reworked

parts.note: Aries is the first house of the zodiac in astrology

explanation.surface: What you need at home after some uncomfortable scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: In astrology the zodiac signs are called houses, so 'house' can be ARIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Necessaries are the essentials, the things that are required.
